sentences.text: Aegyptosaurus was a quadrupedal dinosaur featuring a long neck and tail alongside a small skull.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes three tail vertebrae, a partial shoulder blade, and nine limb bones.
Paleontologist Gregory S. Paul estimated this large herbivore reached 15 meters in length, stood 5 meters tall, and weighed 7 tonnes.
German paleontologist Ernst Stromer formally described the genus Aegyptosaurus in 1932.
However, most original specimens were destroyed during an Allied bombing raid on the Munich museum on April 25, 1944.
Aegyptosaurus shared its habitat and time period with large predators such as Carcharodontosaurus and Spinosaurus.
Aegyptosaurus is the only known species of its extinct genus and is classified as a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
It belongs to the parent group Titanosauria.
This dinosaur lived in Africa during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 95 million years ago.
Its time range is estimated from the Berriasian to the Cenomanian, spanning between 143.1 and 93.9 million years ago.
Fossils have been found in the Bahariya Formation in Egypt and the Farak Formation in Niger.
